answer: A desert mesa stays honest when every new identity must carry a distinct umber-painted marker stone up a different mesa trail and set it where a distinct scout fires a signal flare to confirm the climb. The first fake owes one stone, the second two, the third three, so twenty fakes owe 210 stones carried one at a time. Bulk farming fails because the narrow trail admits a single climber per ascent and each stone weighs a full day's carry, like one mule hauling one load per trip up the mesa. The tenth fake alone owes ten stones, and the trail only grows steeper.
